title: 135 Farm characteristics, challenges, and perspectives of meat-goat producers in the Southeast US
content:
Abstract
Understanding farm characteristics, challenges, and producers’ perspective regarding the operation and related aspects of the enterprise is essential for designing suitable research and extension programs and delivering them successfully. However, little information is available about meat-goat producers from the Southeast. The objective of this study was to explore farm characteristics and understand the challenges and perspectives of meat-goat producers from the southeast US. A pre-structured survey questionnaire was developed, pretested, finalized, and shared with producers in the Southeast US using the contact list of the research team and beyond (producers’ organizations, extension personnel working in the Southeastern Land-Grant Universities, commodity groups, non-profit organizations, farmers’ cooperatives, and other organizations). A total of 125 responses were received from producers living in 12 Southeast states. Data were analyzed for descriptive statistics in Microsoft Excel. Respondents included 42% female, 55% male, and the remaining did not wish to disclose. African American (47%) and white (44%) were the major races among the respondents. Thirty-four percent of the respondents had graduate or professional degrees, followed by bachelor’s degree (30%) and high-school diploma (17%). Twenty-nine percent of the respondents have been raising goats for 1-5 years, 22% for 16-20 years, and 21% for 6-10 years. Most respondents were small producers with 39% having 10 or fewer and 29% having 11-25 breeding does. Most producers relied on grazing-based production systems, with pasture-based systems accounting for 79% and ranch-based systems for 14%, and the majority had a land area of 16 ha or less (72%). Income (43%), weed control in large animal pastures (17%), and land clearance (16%) were the top three reasons for raising goats. Lack of established market (21%), internal parasitism (17%), and high cost of hay and supplementary feeds (16%) were the top three challenges listed by the respondents. Forty-two percent of the respondents expressed marketing constraints and 22% thought low sell price for their animals as concerns for sustaining their farms. A few of the marketing problems mentioned were limited hauling capacity (28%), failure to sell (34%), and stockyards or slaughterhouses being far away from their farms (38%). Other than live animals, 34% respondents sold meat and meat products and 8% sold manure or compost. Most of the respondents (79%) mentioned that they consumed goat meat. Forty-four percent expressed that they would continue raising goats life long, followed by 26% who were not sure. and 14% for the next 6-10 years. Results of this study revealed important characteristics of Southeast meat-goat farms and producers and their operational perspectives that can be useful to designing and delivering Extension services. This understanding can then be combined with consumer perspectives to make goat meat a main-stream market product to promote profitability and sustainability in the goat meat industry.
